title: Rounding and Estimation: Decimal Places and Significant Figures
seo_title: Year 7 Rounding Worksheets: Decimal Places, Significant Figures and Estimating Calculations
standard_text: Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy (for example, to a number of decimal places or significant figures); use approximation through rounding to estimate answers and calculate possible resulting errors.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 rounding worksheets: round to decimal places and significant figures, choose the right rounding, and estimate calculations by rounding to 1 significant figure. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Round to 1 significant figure to estimate: 38.7 × 21.4 ≈ 40 × 20 = 800.
key_sub: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit. Keep place-holder zeros: 48,372 ≈ 50,000.
body_html:
How it works

To round, find the last digit you keep, then look at the next digit: 5 or more, round up; 4 or less, keep it.

Decimal places are counted after the point. Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit. When you round a big number, fill the gaps with zeros: 48,372 to 1 s.f. is 50,000.

To estimate, round each number to 1 significant figure, then calculate.

Example

Round 0.04851 to 2 significant figures.

The first significant figure is 4, the second is 8.

The next digit is 5, so round up.

Answer: 0.049

Example

Estimate 38.7 × 21.4.

38.7 ≈ 40 and 21.4 ≈ 20.

40 × 20 = 800.

Answer: 800

Common mistakes

  • Cutting off digits instead of rounding: 2.347 to 1 d.p. is 2.3, but 2.36 is 2.4.
  • Counting zeros at the start as significant figures: 0.0076 to 1 s.f. is 0.008.
  • Dropping place-holder zeros: 48,372 to 1 s.f. is 50,000, not 5.
  • Leaving off a final zero: 9.97 to 1 d.p. is 10.0, not 10.

faq.q: What is the difference between decimal places and significant figures?
faq.a: Decimal places are counted after the decimal point. Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit, which may be before the point.
Zeros at the start, as in 0.0076, are not. Zeros between other digits, as in 4,05, are. Zeros at the end of a rounded whole number are place holders.
To check that a calculator answer is sensible. If 38.7 × 21.4 should be about 800, then 8,281.8 must be wrong.

faq.q: What do I do when the next digit is 5?
faq.a: Round up. 2.45 to 1 decimal place is 2.5.
